title: Telling the time
goal: By the end of this lesson you can ask and tell the time, use et quart, et demie and moins quart, say midi and minuit, read 24-hour times on Quebec schedules (15 h 30), and give the time of an event with à.

body: Ask *Quelle heure est-il?* (standard) or *Il est quelle heure?* (casual). Answer with *Il est* + number + *heure(s)*: *Il est trois heures.* *Heure* is feminine, so 1 o'clock is *une heure*.
Minutes simply follow the hour: *Il est trois heures dix* (3:10), *Il est huit heures vingt-cinq* (8:25).
learn.tip: Always say heures: 'il est trois' alone is incomplete.

body: *et quart* = quarter past, *et demie* = half past, *moins le quart* = quarter to. For other minutes before the hour, use *moins*: *Il est cinq heures moins dix* (4:50, literally 'five minus ten').
In Quebec, *moins quart* (without *le*) is very common: *Il est trois heures moins quart.*

head: Time
French

learn.h: Midi, minuit, and parts of the day
body: Noon is *midi* and midnight is *minuit*. Both are masculine and have no *heures*: *Il est midi. Il est minuit et quart.* Half past noon: *midi et demi* (no -e, because midi is masculine).
In conversation, the 12-hour clock is normal, with *du matin* (a.m.), *de l'après-midi* (afternoon) or *du soir* (evening): *trois heures de l'après-midi*, *huit heures du soir*.

Schedules, tickets, store hours and official announcements in Quebec use the 24-hour clock, written with *h* and spaces: *15 h 30* is said *quinze heures trente*. With the 24-hour clock, use numbers only: no *et quart*, *et demie* or *moins*.
To say when something happens, use *à*: *Le film commence à vingt heures* (at 8 p.m.). *De … à …* gives a range: *Le magasin est ouvert de 9 h à 21 h.*
learn.tip: Quebec writes 15 h 30, not 15:30 or 3:30 PM.

body: Quebec speech uses the 12-hour clock with *du matin / de l'après-midi / du soir*, and *moins quart* without *le*. You'll also hear *Il est quelle heure?* far more than *Quelle heure est-il?*
Casual pronunciation shortens *il est* to *y'é* or *il'é*, and *heures* gets swallowed: *Y'é trois heures* sounds like 'yé trwa-zeur'. Expect quick times in the métro and at work.

quebec.intro: In Quebec, schedules and signs use the 24-hour clock (15 h 30), but people talk in the 12-hour clock with du matin / du soir. Midi and minuit replace 12 o'clock, and moins quart usually drops le.

items.std: Il est trois heures moins le quart.

items.qc: Il est trois heures de l'après-midi.
items.note: 24 h on signs, 12 h in conversation
